features.label: Median slope
features.description: Median slope of the 20 km block (Earth) or region (Moon) at a 40 m baseline. Same slope code on Copernicus GLO-30 and LRO LOLA.

features.label: Roughness
features.description: Median residual height after fitting a plane in each 3 by 3 window (about 120 m wide), same code on both bodies.

features.label: Relief
features.description: Elevation range inside the block: 5th to 95th percentile. Moon regions range from 1.2 to 5.1 km.

features.label: Landing-flat share (< 10 deg)
features.description: Share of the block with slope under 10 degrees at 40 m, a rough proxy for landable ground.

features.label: Crater-like pits
features.description: Closed depressions per km2 found by the same detector on both bodies. Earth blocks have few (0 to 0.03 typical), Moon regions 0.04 to 0.21.

features.label: Shadowed share, sun 1.5 deg
features.description: Share of the block that never sees a sun 1.5 degrees above the horizon in any direction, a proxy for permanent shadow under the low polar sun.

features.label: Mean surface temperature
features.description: Annual mean land surface temperature. Earth: MODIS MYD11A2 (2019 to 2023). Moon: Diviner annual average, median over the region. The gap is large: Moon 105 to 153 K, Earth blocks about 250 to 297 K.

features.label: Max surface temperature
features.description: Earth: 95th percentile of MODIS daytime land surface temperature. Moon: median of the Diviner maximum over the region. Different statistics, so compare loosely.

features.label: Ice / frozen-ground proxy
features.description: Not the same quantity on both bodies. Earth: share of MODIS observations that are frozen. Moon: share of the region where Diviner temperatures allow ice to be stable within the top metre or so. Read it as 'how ice-friendly', not as ice amount.

features.label: Precipitation
features.description: Earth: NASA POWER climatology (mm per day times 365). Moon: 0.

features.label: Vegetation (NDVI max)
features.description: Peak NDVI in 2019 to 2023 from MODIS MYD13Q1 on Earth; 0 on the Moon. Values above about 0.2 mean sparse to dense plant cover.

features.label: Snow cover share
features.description: Share of valid MODIS MYD10A2 observations with snow (Earth); 0 on the Moon.

datasets.name: Copernicus GLO-30 DEM
datasets.notes: 235 tiles shortlisted for cold, dry, rugged terrain; resampled to 40 m, cut into 20 by 20 km blocks.

datasets.name: LRO LOLA LDEM_80S_40M
datasets.notes: Moon slope, roughness, relief, crater-like pits, landing share, shadow structure.

datasets.name: LRO Diviner polar resource products (PRP)
datasets.notes: Annual mean and maximum temperature, ice-stability fractions per region.

datasets.name: MODIS MYD11A2 land surface temperature
datasets.notes: Read anonymously via Microsoft Planetary Computer. Annual mean, daytime 95th percentile, frozen-observation share.

datasets.name: MODIS MYD10A2 snow cover
datasets.notes: Share of valid observations with snow.

datasets.name: NASA POWER climatology
datasets.notes: Precipitation in mm per day, multiplied by 365.

provenance.processing: Twelve features shared by Earth blocks and Moon regions. Terrain features come from the same slope, roughness and depression code run on Copernicus GLO-30 (resampled to 40 m) and on LOLA 40 m. Climate features are MODIS and NASA POWER on Earth and Diviner on the Moon. ice_proxy and temp_max_k use different statistics on each body (see descriptions). Norm ranges are fixed so that Moon and Earth values both fall on-scale.
